projects.title: Magnolia house, basement ADU and garage
projects.card: Remodel of a one-story house over a daylight basement, with a new 865 SF basement ADU and a detached one-car garage.
projects.firstLine: The finished house, the ADU below it, and the garage. Choose Explore to turn the model or go to a room.
projects.dek: Explore the Magnolia project layer by layer: the finished house, the roof, the main level, the basement ADU and the foundation.
projects.sourceNote: Traced from the permit sets. Unprinted dimensions are scaled by eye from the sheets.

projects.title: One-story house with shop and garage
projects.card: A one-story layout, 6,720 SF total as printed: primary suite, two bedrooms, open kitchen, living and dining with a 14 foot ceiling, a den, and a large attached garage with a shop.
projects.dek: Explore this one-story layout layer by layer: the finished house, the roof, the floor plan with every room, and the slab.
projects.sourceNote: Modeled from a one-page layout plan. Walls, openings, room names, areas and ceiling heights come from the plan. The roof, window sills and heads, and door heights are not drawn on the plan and are shown as labeled assumptions.
assumptions: Roof: not drawn on the layout. Assumed hipped roofs at 4:12 with 18 inch overhangs over every wing, meeting in hips and valleys.

Garage and shop walls are assumed at 16 feet; the layout prints no garage ceiling height. The whole garage and shop wing shares one roof with one ridge height: past the 16 foot wide north bay's ridge line the slope eases to a 1/2:12 deck, so nothing steps down mid garage.
The house roof sits on its 9 foot walls and rises into the taller garage wall, so no pocket is left where they meet, and stays clear of the rear garage door by the walk-in closet.
The covered patio roof runs unbroken along the whole north face at the 9 foot eave. The living and dining room roof is raised behind it over the 14 foot ceiling, with short clerestory walls.
The layout prints 9 foot ceilings for the Primary Bedroom, Kitchen and Den, so those walls stay at 9 feet.
Dining and sink bay sizes are scaled from the layout; bay sills and the bay roof height are assumed.
Exterior door leaves are shown at an assumed 6 foot 8 inch height; the Primary Bedroom corner doors are shown as glazed French doors.

projects.title: Two-story house with attached garage
projects.card: A two-story house from an approved permit set, 3,063 SF conditioned: open dining, kitchen and living under a 10 foot ceiling, a dining room open to the floor above, a primary suite, two bedrooms, two offices and a 12 foot garage.
projects.dek: Explore this two-story house layer by layer: the finished house, the roof, the upper floor, the main floor with every room, and the slab.
projects.sourceNote: Modeled from the approved permit set: both floor plans, the roof plan, four elevations, the building section and the window and door schedules. Walls, openings, room names, areas, ceiling heights, roof pitches and the overall height come from those sheets. Anything the sheets do not print is listed below as an assumption.

roof: From the roof plan and elevations: a 5:12 main gable, a 10:12 cross gable with gable ends on both sides, a 9 5/8:12 gable over the garage, an 11:12 dormer gable and a 5:12 porch roof on three posts. Overhangs are 18 inches and the roofing is asphalt shingle. The highest point is 32'-2" above average grade, as printed.
garage: The garage is 460 SF with a 12 foot ceiling. Its slab sits three risers below the main floor, with a 16 by 7 foot overhead door and a side door.
header: Window and door sizes come from the schedules and sit in the wall gaps drawn on the plans. Heads are set at 6'-8" to line up with the doors, as the elevations show; sills follow from each scheduled window height.
partition: Room names, areas and ceiling heights are the ones printed on the plans: 10 feet on the main floor, 9 feet upstairs and 12 feet in the garage. The dining room is open to the upper floor. Select a room to fly in.
foundation: A slab on grade under the main floor, and the garage slab three risers lower.

assumptions: Window heads at 6'-8" are scaled from the elevations, where they line up with the door heads. Sills are the head minus the scheduled window height.
Upper floor framing is drawn 1'-6" deep, scaled from the elevation level lines.
The main floor sits 1'-11" above the garage slab (three printed risers at 7 3/4 inches). The ground is drawn flat at the garage slab.
Dormer eave and porch roof heights are scaled from the south and west elevations.
The stair is drawn as a straight run of 18 risers at the printed 7 3/4 inch rise. The turn at its foot is simplified.
Furniture and fixtures sit where the plan symbols are, scaled from the drawing. Interior doors are shown as open frames.

The plan examiner's markups on the approved set are applied: the laundry wall moved 1'-6" west, the Office 01 door moved to the hall side, an upstairs door replaced by a 40 inch archway into the primary bedroom, a floor to ceiling window on the main floor north wall, and the larger side patio.
The markups print only 1'-6", 18' and 40 inches. The moved office door, the archway, the new window and the patio's diagonal edge are scaled from the hand sketch and may be off by several inches.
The floor to ceiling window runs from the floor to 9'-6". Its head height is not printed.

Room areas are the printed ones, except the upstairs laundry. Its area was printed as 75.84 SF before the markup moved its wall, so the label shows the redlined area as modeled, about 96 SF. The open living room and the two halls have no drawn boundaries, so their outlines are approximate.
Siding, stone veneer, deck and porch railings and trim colors are not modeled.

projects.title: One-story house with a new second story
projects.card: A second-story addition from a plan set: a full new upper floor over an existing one-story house, with a primary suite, two bedrooms, two baths and a storage room under one 6:12 gable roof. The first floor keeps its rooms and gains a mudroom and a new stair.
projects.dek: Explore the addition layer by layer: the finished house, the roof, the new second floor, the existing first floor with its new mudroom and stair, and the floor platform.
projects.sourceNote: Modeled from the plan set: the proposed first and second floor plans, the roof plan and four proposed elevations. Walls, openings, room names, the printed areas, floor and plate heights, the roof pitch and the overhangs come from those sheets. Anything the sheets do not print is listed below as an assumption.

roof: From the roof plan and elevations: one 6:12 gable over the whole house, with its gable ends on the deck side and the shed side, 18 inch overhangs and asphalt shingles. The new wall plate is printed at 17'-0" above the first floor, so the ridge sits about 23'-5" above it.
header: New windows and doors use the sizes printed beside them on the plans, such as 72 by 60 inch bedroom windows and 30 by 80 inch doors. Existing first floor openings are only marked existing, so their widths are the wall gaps on the plan and their heights are scaled from the elevations.
partition: Second floor rooms show their printed areas, with 9 foot walls between the printed 8'-0" second floor and the 17'-0" plate. The existing first floor rooms have no printed areas, so they show names only. Select a room to fly in.

assumptions: The overall size, 25'-8" by 41'-2", is printed with a note to verify it in the field. Walls are traced from the plan linework at 1/4 inch = 1 foot.
The first floor sits 2 feet above the ground, scaled from the deck skirt and stair on the deck-side elevation. The site slope is not modeled; the ground is drawn flat.

First floor walls run the printed 8'-0" from the first floor to the second floor. The first floor ceiling height and the floor framing depth are not printed; the framing is drawn about 11 inches deep.

Window heads are scaled from the elevations: about 7'-0" on the first floor and 8'-0" above the second floor. Sills follow from the printed window heights. Existing first floor windows are drawn 4 feet tall, scaled.
The second floor stair window has no printed size. It is drawn 3 by 5 feet, scaled from the elevation.
Existing first floor openings are marked existing without sizes. Their widths are the wall gaps on the plan, and door heads are 6'-8".
The ridge height is not printed. It follows from the printed 17'-0" plate and the 6:12 pitch.
The stair is drawn as two straight flights with a landing, 15 risers in all. The riser count is not printed; the plans note a 7 inch maximum riser.
The existing shed and its roof stay as they are. Their heights are scaled from the elevations.
Existing first floor rooms have no printed areas, so their labels show names only.
Furniture and fixtures sit where the plan symbols are, scaled from the drawing. Interior doors are shown as open frames.
Siding, trim, deck railings and exterior lights are not modeled.

projects.title: Hillside post-and-beam house with a lower-level ADU
projects.card: Preliminary design for a new custom post-and-beam home on a sloping lot: a main floor with a planted roof, a primary suite upstairs and a daylight lower-level ADU with two bedrooms that opens to the back patio.
projects.dek: Explore the preliminary design layer by layer: the house on its slope, the entry side, the flat and planted roofs, the upper floor, the main floor and the lower-level ADU.
projects.sourceNote: Preliminary design, modeled from the design drawings: the main, upper and lower level plans at 1/8 inch = 1 foot, four elevations and the 3D plan views. Walls, wall openings, room names, the level areas, the floor to floor heights and the roof outline come from those sheets. The design may still change. Anything the sheets do not print is listed below as an assumption.

roof: From the elevations and the 3D views: two flat, low roofs with deep overhangs, one over the main floor and one over the upper floor. The main roof outline is drawn on the upper level plan, where it is labeled green roof. The back elevation prints three 10'-6" steps, so the main roof sits 10'-6" above the main floor and the upper roof 10'-6" above the upper floor.
header: Window and door widths are the gaps in the exterior walls on the plans, mostly 4'-11" bays between the posts of the 5'-6" building grid. The plans print no window schedule, so sills and heads are scaled from the elevations by window type: tall glass to the back, high transom windows on the street sides.
partition: The plans print the area of each level but no room areas, so rooms show their names only. Select a room to fly in.

assumptions: This is a preliminary design. The drawings say the design may change.
Walls are traced from the plan drawings at 1/8 inch = 1 foot, checked against the printed 5'-6" building grid. No overall dimensions are printed.
Floor to floor heights are the printed 10'-6" steps on the back elevation. Walls stop 1'-0" below the next level for the roof and floor edge; that depth is scaled from the elevations.
Window and door heights are scaled from the elevations by window type. There is no window or door schedule.

The main roof outline is the line drawn on the upper level plan. The upper roof overhang, about 2'-0", is scaled from the elevations. Both roofs are drawn flat; their slope for drainage is not printed.
The green roof is drawn over the whole main roof outside the upper floor, as the upper level plan labels it. Planting and parapet details are not shown.

The ground is drawn as simple planes scaled from the side elevations: level with the lower floor behind the house, rising to the main floor on the street side, and stepping down beside the walk stair to the lower level entry. The lot shape, the full 16 foot fall across the lot and any retaining walls are not modeled.
The stairs are drawn as straight flights of 17 risers, scaled from the plans. The riser count is not printed.
The walk steps between the lower entry and the main level walk are the nine treads drawn on the plans; their rise is assumed even.
Two rooms with no printed name are labeled Bath (unlabeled) from their plumbing fixtures.
The main deck posts are placed at its outer corners, scaled from the back elevation. Railings are not modeled.
Furniture and fixtures sit where the plan symbols are, scaled from the drawing. Interior doors are shown as open gaps.
Siding, cedar trim, posts and beams inside the glass walls, and window mullions are not modeled.
